Australia Takes Lead as Day 3 of WTC Decider Turns in Their Favor

04 Nov 2026, 02:18 PM IST · GlobeWire Daily Editorial Desk · Source: www.icc-cricket.com

2 min read

Key takeaways--- All quoted statements are taken from player interviews reported by the ICC after Day 3.

Image: icc · Photo source · Resized and letterboxed to 16:9; no AI generation

In this article
  1. Match Overview
  2. Key Performances
  3. Implications for the World Test Championship
  4. How to Verify the Information

Match Overview

  • Competition: ICC World Test Championship (2021‑2023 cycle) – final series
  • Teams: Australia vs South Africa
  • Venue: Newlands, Cape Town, South Africa
  • Dates: 27 – 31 October 2023 (Day 3 played on 29 October, local time GMT+2)
  • Format: Five‑day Test match, part of the WTC points race. The series is tied 1‑1, so the third Test decides the championship.
  • Current status: Australia finished Day 3 with a 40‑run lead in South Africa’s second innings. South Africa are 140/4 with Matthew Breetzke (19*) and Ryan Rickelton (8*) at the crease.

Key Performances

  • Nathan Lyon dismissed South Africa captain Temba Bavuma in the pen‑ultimate over of the day, a turning point that gave Australia a psychological edge.
  • Josh Inglis (Australia) completed a maiden Test century, finishing on 108 and describing the session as a “controlled tempo” where the bowlers “looked threatening the whole time.”
  • Alex Carey added a solid 80 runs, supporting Inglis’s effort.
  • Simon Harmer (South Africa) took 4/104 and noted that the pitch had changed dramatically, suggesting spin could become more influential over the final two days.
  • Marco Jansen claimed 3/60, continuing his strong series showing.
  • Mitchell Starc and Josh Hazlewood (Australia) each took early wickets in South Africa’s first innings, helping Australia recover from a 100‑run deficit.

Implications for the World Test Championship

  • With the series level at 1‑1, the third Test is effectively a championship final. Australia’s current lead puts them in a position to press for a win and clinch the title.
  • The spin‑friendly conditions highlighted by Harmer could shift the balance if South Africa rebuilds a partnership. Conversely, Australia’s pace attack, especially Starc’s ability to generate foot‑marks, remains a threat.
  • A win for Australia would give them the series 2‑1 and the WTC trophy; a South African comeback could force a tie‑breaker based on points‑per‑match, as per ICC regulations.

How to Verify the Information

  • The ICC’s official website (icc-cricket.com) provides live scores, match reports, and the full scoreboard for the Cape Town Test.
  • Reputable sports news outlets such as ESPNcricinfo and BBC Sport update the match status in real time and publish post‑match analyses.
  • Video highlights and commentary are available on the ICC’s YouTube channel and the broadcasters’ streaming platforms (e.g., Sky Sports, SuperSport).
